Reproducing Okuno et al. (2025) from dandiset 000727¶

Paper. Okuno T, Woodward A, Okano H, Hata J (2025). Functional connectivity, structural connectivity, and inter-individual variability in Drosophila melanogaster. eLife reviewed preprint 107990 version 1, doi:10.7554/elife.107990.1. The claims file was written from the publisher's HTML of version 1 (main text, Methods, figure legends and the legends of the Extended Data figures); no PDF was available.

Dandiset. DANDI:000727, version 0.240106.0043, the version the paper's Methods and Data availability cite. It is also the only published version; the draft lists the same 18 assets with the same total size.

What the dandiset holds. The whole-brain two-photon imaging of Brezovec et al. that the paper reuses: 9 flies, one NWB file each, with the raw GCaMP6f and tdTomato volumes (256 x 128 x 49 voxels, 3384 volumes at 1.88 Hz), anatomical stacks, a green series already registered to the FDA space by Brezovec et al. (high-pass filtered and z-scored), and FicTrac walking data at 50 Hz.

Outside inputs (the claims file says the paper relies on them; both are pinned):

  • the paper's code, github.com/takuto-okuno-riken/flywalk at commit 4b92add: the resized FDA template, brain mask, the hemibrain neuropil atlas (114 ROIs), the JFRC2010 atlas, the FlyEM cf0.8 SC of the 114 ROIs and the walking regressors it computed (data/behavior.mat);
  • the paper's Zenodo record 10.5281/zenodo.15532272 (version of 2025-05-28, the one the code's README cites; the later version 18151010 postdates the preprint): FlyWire sc140 SC of the hemibrain ROIs, the selected-synapse SC matrices, the 99 null SC matrices of each permutation test, per-ROI transmitter and post-synapse counts.

The SCKm and DistKm ROI atlases (k-means parcellations) are in neither, so every claim on them is blocked. The analysis streams each fly's raw green series once for FC and once for the GLM.

dandiset 000727 version 0.240106.0043
code commit 4b92add4a44f641ab6add809ff6b0e0d6110b50c zenodo record 15532272

Data check¶

The files, their metadata, and what the analysis reads from them. ANTs registration draws random samples. antspy 0.6.3 ignores the random_seed argument of ants.registration (it falls into **kwargs), so the earlier runs of this attempt were unseeded and their registrations, and every number resting on them, changed from run to run. The seed is now set through ants.config and ITK runs on one thread; the orientation cell below registers one mean image twice with the same seed to show that the result repeats. A registration with another seed (11) is a different local optimum, and how far it moves the voxels and the results is shown for every fly (cell after the reduction). No other random numbers are drawn.

In [2]:
assets = flyfc.list_assets()
print(len(assets), "NWB files")
meta = []
for a in assets:
    h5 = flyfc.open_nwb(a["s3"])
    g = h5[flyfc.GREEN]
    st = h5["acquisition/TwoPhotonSeriesFunctionalGreen/starting_time"]
    gs = h5["general/optophysiology/ImagingPlaneGCaMP6fFunctional/grid_spacing"][()]
    spd = h5["processing/behavior/FicTrac/SpatialSeriesMovementSpeed"]
    proc = h5["processing/ophys/TwoPhotonSeriesFunctionalGreenProcessed/data"]
    row = dict(subject=a["subject"], size_gb=round(a["size"] / 1e9, 1), green=g.shape, dtype=str(g.dtype),
               rate=round(float(st.attrs["rate"]), 6), spacing_um=tuple(np.round(gs * 1e6, 3)),
               speed_n=spd["data"].shape[0], speed_rate=float(spd["starting_time"].attrs["rate"]),
               speed_desc=spd.attrs["description"], processed=proc.shape,
               sex=h5["general/subject/sex"][()].decode(),
               genotype=h5["general/subject/genotype"][()].decode())
    meta.append(row)
    h5.close()
for r in meta:
    print(r["subject"], r["size_gb"], "GB green", r["green"], r["dtype"], "rate", r["rate"], "Hz spacing", r["spacing_um"],
          "um | speed", r["speed_n"], "samples at", r["speed_rate"], "Hz | processed", r["processed"], "|", r["sex"])
print("genotypes:", sorted({r["genotype"] for r in meta}))
print("speed description:", meta[0]["speed_desc"])
print("imaging duration (s):", sorted({round(r["green"][0] / r["rate"], 1) for r in meta}),
      "behaviour duration (s):", sorted({r["speed_n"] / r["speed_rate"] for r in meta}))

Orientation and registration. The template and the masks come from the paper's code. The native mean image of the first fly is shown beside the template, and the correlation with the template after an affine registration is printed for each of the eight axis flips. The first fly's mean image is registered twice with seed 1 to show that a seeded registration repeats.

In [3]:
tm, tz = flyfc.code_nifti("template/thresholded_FDACal.nii.gz")
tmpl = ants.from_numpy(tm, spacing=tuple(float(v) / 1000 for v in tz))
brain, _ = flyfc.code_nifti("template/thresholded_FDACal_mask.nii.gz")
brain = brain > 0
masks = flyfc.hemiroi_masks()
names = flyfc.hemiroi_names()
print("template", tm.shape, "voxel (um)", tuple(round(float(v), 3) for v in tz), "brain-mask voxels", int(brain.sum()))
print("hemibrain ROIs", len(masks), "voxels per ROI", min(int(m.sum()) for m in masks), "to", max(int(m.sum()) for m in masks))

h5 = flyfc.open_nwb(assets[0]["s3"])
rd0 = flyfc.ChunkReader(assets[0]["s3"], h5)
T0 = rd0.shape[0]; ct = rd0.chunks[0]
mean0 = rd0.mean_image({0, ct * ((T0 // ct) // 2), ct * ((T0 - 1) // ct)})
vox0 = flyfc.spacing_mm(h5)
h5.close()
flips = flyfc.choose_flip(mean0, tmpl, vox0)
for k, v in flips.items():
    print("flip", k, "affine correlation with template", round(v, 3))
fig, ax = plt.subplots(2, 4, figsize=(15, 5))
for i, z in enumerate([6, 18, 30, 42]):
    ax[0, i].imshow(mean0[:, :, z].T, cmap="gray"); ax[0, i].set_title(f"{assets[0]['subject']} native z={z}")
    ax[1, i].imshow(tm[:, :, z].T, cmap="gray"); ax[1, i].set_title(f"template z={z}")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
print("native mean image range", mean0.min().round(1), mean0.max().round(1), "| template range", tm.min(), tm.max().round(3))
# repeatability: the same mean image registered twice with seed 1
c_a, cc_a, _ = flyfc.register(mean0, tmpl, (1, 1, 1), vox0, seed=1)
c_b, cc_b, _ = flyfc.register(mean0, tmpl, (1, 1, 1), vox0, seed=1)
ok_ = ~np.isnan(c_a).any(1) & ~np.isnan(c_b).any(1)
print("two registrations with seed 1: largest coordinate difference", float(np.abs(c_a[ok_] - c_b[ok_]).max()),
      "native voxels | same field of view:", bool((np.isnan(c_a).any(1) == np.isnan(c_b).any(1)).all()), "| SyN correlation", round(cc_a["syn"], 4), round(cc_b["syn"], 4))

In both images the slices near z = 6 hold two small dorsal-anterior structures near the midline and the slices near z = 42 hold the optic lobes, and the dorsoventral axis runs the same way, so no flip is applied along y or z. Left and right cannot be told apart from the image, and the affine correlations printed above are not a reliable guide: antspy's default affine stage favours flips along y and z, which the images rule out. No flip is assumed; the main FC-SC results are shown with left and right ROIs swapped, and the orientation is checked against the paper's own per-region FC-SC values (fig3e section) and its deposited GLM map (GLM section). The two checks disagree.

Reduce each fly. Each fly's raw green series is streamed once (about 7 GB per fly) and reduced to the 114 ROI mean series and the 1000 highest-SD voxels (flyfc.process_fly), and the middle 20 slices of the tdTomato series are read for the motion estimate.

flies = []
for a in assets:
    f = flyfc.process_fly(a, tmpl, masks, repeats=(11,))
    f.pop("warped"); f.pop("mean")
    flies.append(f)
    print(f["subject"], "read", round(f["mb_read"]), "MB in", round(f["t_total"]), "s | correlation with template",
          {k: round(v, 3) for k, v in f["cc"].items()}, "| voxel (um)", tuple(round(v * 1000, 3) for v in f["vox"]), "| ROIs not fully in the field of view",
          int((f["cover"] < 0.999).sum()), "min coverage", round(float(np.nanmin(f["cover"])), 3), flush=True)
print("peak memory (GB)", round(resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss / 1e6, 2), "| elapsed (min)", round((time.time() - T_START) / 60, 1))

Subject order and the behaviour clock. The paper's code holds the per-volume speed and the walking regressor it computed for its nine flies (data/behavior.mat). Computing them from the dandiset's FicTrac speed, with the code's offset of 104.654892 ms, and comparing fly by fly checks both the subject order and the alignment of the behaviour to the volumes.

In [7]:
reg, mscal, th_speed, b_speed = flyfc.walking_regressors([f["speed"] for f in flies])
reg_bin, _, _, _ = flyfc.walking_regressors([f["speed"] for f in flies], binary=True)
beh = flyfc.load_mat(flyfc.code_file("data/behavior.mat"))
M = np.asarray(beh["MScal"], float); M2 = np.asarray(beh["MBcal2"], float)
print("code's MScal", M.shape, "| th (mean SD of speed)", round(th_speed, 5), "b (mean 10th percentile)", round(b_speed, 5))
C = np.array([[np.corrcoef(mscal[i], M[j])[0, 1] for j in range(9)] for i in range(9)])
for i, f in enumerate(flies):
    print(f["subject"], "best-matching code fly", int(np.argmax(C[i])) + 1, "r", round(C[i].max(), 6),
          "| max |speed diff|", f"{np.abs(mscal[i] - M[i]).max():.2e}", "| regressor max |diff|", f"{np.abs(reg[i] - M2[i]).max():.2e}")
print("speed range", round(min(f["speed"].min() for f in flies), 4), "to", round(max(f["speed"].max() for f in flies), 4), "(radians per frame, as the file states)")
print("fraction of volumes at or above b + th (binary walking):", np.round((mscal >= b_speed + th_speed).mean(1), 3))

The behaviour clock is checked against the imaging with a contrast: the brain-wide mean of the ROI series, after removing the 7 polynomial terms, against the walking regressor, at shifts of the regressor by -60 to 60 volumes. If the two streams share the clock, the correlation peaks near shift 0 (the regressor is already convolved with the calcium response).

In [8]:
shifts = np.arange(-60, 61, 2)
ids_all = np.arange(114)
for i, f in enumerate(flies):
    g = flyfc.residualize(f["R"][ids_all].mean(0)[:, None], flyfc.poly_regressors(f["T"]))[:, 0]
    cc = [np.corrcoef(np.roll(reg[i], s)[70:-70], g[70:-70])[0, 1] for s in shifts]
    k = int(np.argmax(cc))
    print(f["subject"], "peak r", round(cc[k], 3), "at shift", int(shifts[k]), "volumes | r at 0:", round(cc[30], 3),
          "| median |r| at shifts beyond 30:", round(float(np.median(np.abs(np.array(cc)[np.abs(shifts) > 30]))), 3))

Motion. The paper corrects motion and slice timing with SPM12 before registration (Methods, Preprocessing; claims file M1); this attempt does neither. To show whether the raw series moves, each volume's sum over the middle 20 slices (z = 15 to 34) of the structural tdTomato channel is aligned to the mean over volumes by cross-correlation, giving a rigid in-plane shift per volume (flyfc.inplane_shift; it cannot see motion along z). The same from the green channel's sum over all slices is printed beside it. The shift is compared with the voxel size and with walking, and fig3d is recomputed with the two tdTomato shift series added to the nuisance regressors (fig3d section).

FC and the paper's SC¶

FC per fly is the Pearson correlation of the 114 ROI series, Fisher-z transformed and averaged over the code's eight flies (M3). Poly-tCompCor is the 7 polynomial terms and 6 tCompCor components; tCompCor is taken from the 1000 native voxels with the highest temporal SD (an assumption: the code takes them among template voxels, after warping). SC is the second ("Traced") layer of each connect list (M4).

Result: FlyEM gives the higher FC-SC correlation, but both values are below the paper's. With the code's eight flies and Poly-tCompCor, r is 0.606 for FlyEM and 0.566 for FlyWire, below the lower bounds of the tolerances (0.657 and 0.612), so the claim is partially reproduced. FlyEM is higher in every variant: no nuisance removal 0.636 against 0.597, nine flies 0.601 against 0.562, signed FC the same as the main values, synapse SC 0.553 against 0.524, left and right swapped 0.518 against 0.508, the second registration (seed 11) 0.592 against 0.554, and with the two tdTomato in-plane shift series added to the nuisance regressors 0.611 against 0.571. The paper's own output file for the FlyWire setting gives 0.684 with the same SC, so the gap is in this attempt's FC, not in the SC. No SPM12 motion or slice-timing correction was applied; the raw series moves by about one voxel in plane (motion cell), and regressing the shifts out raises both values by 0.005 only, which leaves them below tolerance. It does not stand in for a realignment.

Result: reproduced, resting on the left-right orientation and close to the bound. FlyEM is higher in 55 of 63 regions under the main setting (tolerance 52.2 to 63.8), 54 with nine flies and 55 with the second registration (seed 11). With left and right swapped the count is 47, and without nuisance removal it is 51, both outside the tolerance. The registration is unstable: the seed 11 registration moves native voxels by a median of 2.5 to 44 um per fly (data check), and the earlier, unseeded runs of this attempt gave 53, 54 and 55. Every registration so far has given 53 to 56, one to four regions above the bound, so the outcome holds across them with little margin. The orientation used is supported by the paper's own per-region FlyWire values: they correlate with this attempt's at r = 0.661 as registered and 0.407 with left and right swapped. The GLM comparison points the other way, more weakly (GLM section).

Result: not reproduced. With this attempt's FC the per-region FC-SC correlation does not rise with the cholinergic share (r = -0.040, p = 0.76) and its relation to the GABAergic share is not significant (r = -0.096, p = 0.46); no variant gives a significant ACh or GABA correlation. The paper's own per-region values from its Zenodo file, run through the same transmitter table, give the paper's numbers (ACh r = 0.395, p = 0.0014; GABA r = -0.252, p = 0.047), so the difference comes from the FC computed here, not from the transmitter table.

Permutation tests: fig4e-unsegregated-higher, fig4f-segregated-lower, fig4i-reciprocal-higher¶

The SC matrix of unsegregated synapses (cPPSSI 0 to 0.1) has a significantly higher FC-SC correlation than 99 random synapse samples of matched size, for both neuron and synapse SC.

The SC matrix of highly segregated synapses (cPPSSI 0.9 to 1) has a significantly lower FC-SC correlation than random synapse samples.

The SC matrix of reciprocal synapses within 2 um has a significantly higher FC-SC correlation than random synapse samples.

M6: the selected SC against the 99 null SC matrices the code pairs with it (rd185-20, rd1560-80, rd140-15), a normal fitted to the null values, two-tailed p, threshold 0.05/6. The null totals are checked against the selected total in the same way.

perm_res = {}
for claim, tgt, null in [("fig4e-unsegregated-higher", "sp10db3000mi1_only1", "rd185-20"),
                         ("fig4f-segregated-lower", "sp90db3000mi1", "rd1560-80"),
                         ("fig4i-reciprocal-higher", "rc20_only1", "rd140-15")]:
    nc, sc, _ = flyfc.load_sc(flyfc.zenodo_member(f"results/sc/hemiroi_fw0sr140_{tgt}_connectlist.mat"))
    nulls = [flyfc.load_sc(flyfc.zenodo_member(f"results/sc/hemiroi_fw0sr140_{null}-{k}_connectlist.mat")) for k in range(1, 100)]
    d = dict(tot=sc[np.ix_(ids, ids)].sum(), ntot=nc[np.ix_(ids, ids)].sum(),
             null_tot=np.array([b[np.ix_(ids, ids)].sum() for a, b, _ in nulls]))
    for lab_, Fx in [("main", F), ("no nuisance", mFz[("", "8")]), ("nine flies", mFz[("poltcomp", "9")]), ("left-right swapped", F[np.ix_(perm, perm)])]:
        r7 = flyfc.fcsc_r(nc, Fx, ids); r9 = flyfc.fcsc_r(sc, Fx, ids)
        n7 = np.array([flyfc.fcsc_r(a, Fx, ids) for a, b, _ in nulls]); n9 = np.array([flyfc.fcsc_r(b, Fx, ids) for a, b, _ in nulls])
        d[lab_] = (r7, n7, r9, n9)
    # the paper's own FC-SC correlations for the same SC matrices (Zenodo auc files, R(7) neuron, R(9) synapse)
    pr = lambda nm: np.ravel(flyfc.load_mat(flyfc.zenodo_member(f"results/auc/poltcomparhemiroi_fw0sr140_{nm}-fcauc.mat"))["R"])
    t_ = pr(tgt); nl = np.array([pr(f"{null}-{k}") for k in range(1, 100)])

          "| totals test p =", round(flyfc.normal_p(d["tot"], d["null_tot"])[0], 3), flush=True)

def show_perm(claim):
    d = perm_res[claim]
    for lab_ in ["paper (deposited R)", "main", "no nuisance", "nine flies", "left-right swapped"]:
        r7, n7, r9, n9 = d[lab_]

        print(f"{lab_:19s} neuron r={r7:.4f} null {m7:.4f}+-{s7:.4f} z={(r7 - m7) / s7:+.1f} p={p7:.3g} "
              f"(null range {n7.min():.4f} to {n7.max():.4f}) | synapse r={r9:.4f} null {m9:.4f}+-{s9:.4f} z={(r9 - m9) / s9:+.1f} p={p9:.3g}")

Result: reproduced. The reciprocal-synapse SC has a higher FC-SC correlation than the null for neuron SC (0.629 against 0.590, z = +24.1) and synapse SC (0.574 against 0.564, z = +4.3, p = 1.5e-5, below 0.05/6); the paper's deposited values give z = +24.8 and +11.8. Nine flies agree. Without nuisance removal the neuron SC is not different from the null (p = 0.94) and the synapse SC is below it (z = -4.8, p = 1.3e-6); with left and right swapped the synapse SC is below it too (z = -3.1, p = 0.002). The synapse part therefore rests on the nuisance removal and the orientation.

GLM of walking: fig5b-walking-activation and fig5b-walking-suppression¶

In the group GLM of walking, the LAL, FB, IPS and GNG neuropils show strong activity.

The Wedge and AVLP neuropils are inactive or strongly suppressed during walking.

M8: the code's graded walking regressor (reproduced exactly above), 7 polynomial terms and 6 tCompCor components; smoothing FWHM 8 voxels; second level on the walking and tCompCor betas of the nine flies (glmFlyMB2nd.m), height threshold p < 0.001. Assumptions: OLS without the Tukey-taper pre-whitening, betas mapped to the template and smoothed there (equal to fitting the warped, smoothed data under OLS), tCompCor from native voxels. The binary regressor (O1) is a variant. Cluster extent: the code's README prints k = 167.9 voxels as its extent threshold, which is used here (18-connectivity, SPM's default).

def neuropil_table(T, th, atlas):
    rows = []
    if atlas == "hemibrain":
        for i in ids:
            m = masks[i] & brain
            if m.sum():
                rows.append((names[i], m))
    else:
        for k in np.unique(jf[jf > 0]).astype(int):
            m = (jf == k) & brain
            if m.sum():
                rows.append((f"{jlab.get(k, k)} [{k}]", m))
    out = []
    for nm, m in rows:
        out.append((nm, float(T[m].mean()), float(T[m].max()), float(T[m].min()), float((T[m] > th).mean()), float((T[m] < -th).mean()), int(m.sum())))
    return out

targets_hb = {"LAL": ["LAL(R)", "LAL(L)"], "FB": ["FB"], "IPS": ["IPS(R)"], "GNG": ["GNG"]}
targets_jf = {"LAL": ["lateral accessory lobe"], "FB": ["fan-shaped body"], "IPS": ["inferior posterior slope"], "GNG": ["adult gnathal ganglion"]}
act = {}
for lab_ in ["graded", "binary"]:
    T, df = glm[lab_]; th = stats.t.isf(0.001, df); tmax = float(T.max())
    lp, sp_ = flyfc.clusters(T > th)
    big = np.isin(lp, 1 + np.nonzero(sp_ >= 168)[0])
    for atlas, tg in [("hemibrain", targets_hb), ("JFRC2010", targets_jf)]:
        tab = neuropil_table(T, th, atlas)
        order = sorted(tab, key=lambda r: -r[1])
        top = {r[0] for r in order[: int(np.ceil(len(order) / 3))]}
        for key, lst in tg.items():
            hits = [r for r in tab if any(r[0].startswith(x) for x in lst)]
            ra = any((big & masks[names.index(r[0])]).any() and r[2] >= tmax / 2 for r in hits) if atlas == "hemibrain" else \
                 any(r[2] >= tmax / 2 for r in hits)
            rb = any(r[0] in top for r in hits)
            act[(lab_, atlas, key)] = (ra, rb)
            print(lab_, atlas, key, "|", "; ".join(f"{r[0]} mean t {r[1]:.2f} max {r[2]:.2f} rank {1 + [o[0] for o in order].index(r[0])}/{len(order)}" for r in hits),
                  "| reading a:", ra, "reading b:", rb)
    print(lab_, "brain-wide max t", round(tmax, 2))

Result: reproduced under reading (a). The second level gives one large positive cluster (404,335 voxels with the graded regressor, 351,796 with the binary one; the paper's deposited map has one of 416,801, printed below) with maximum t = 17.2 (paper 14.7). LAL, FB, IPS and GNG all lie in it with peak t above half the maximum (reading a) under both atlases and both regressors. Reading (b), a mean t in the top third of the neuropils, holds for all four under the hemibrain atlas with both regressors (LAL(L) rank 19 graded and 21 binary, of 63, where the top third ends at 21); under JFRC2010 it fails for LAL (ranks 28 to 32 of 75) and holds for the other three. The per-neuropil mean t correlates with the paper's deposited map at r = 0.41.

The paper's own second level. Its Zenodo record holds the second-level fit of glmFlyMB2nd.m (results/glm/s80poltcomparfly-all-Tukey8full.mat: betas, residual sum of squares, inv(X'X) and trace terms for each brain-mask voxel, with the Tukey taper). Its t map of the walking regressor (lib/calcGlmContrastImage.m) is printed at the README's peaks and over WED and AVLP, and compared voxel by voxel with this attempt's map. The positive clusters of the paper's map are printed, and the orientation is checked twice: voxel by voxel with this attempt's map mirrored (the brain mask nearly matches its own mirror image, so the array mirror is close to a mirror about the midline), and per neuropil with left and right ROIs swapped, the GLM counterpart of the per-region FC check in the fig3e section.

Result: not reproduced. No voxel in the brain mask falls below the negative height threshold (the lowest t is -0.70, -0.68 with the binary regressor), so there is no negative cluster, and 88 to 100% of WED and AVLP voxels are above the positive threshold. The paper's deposited second-level map has the README's two negative clusters (406 and 260 voxels, t = -6.14 and -5.65 at the README peaks), where this attempt has t = 4.37 and 4.68; in the paper's map 58% of AVLP(R) and 88% of WED(R) are also positive-significant. The difference lies in this attempt's preprocessing and GLM (no motion or slice-timing correction, no Tukey taper), not in the data as such.

Orientation. The two maps correlate voxel by voxel at r = 0.359 as registered and 0.394 with this attempt's map mirrored, and per neuropil at 0.41 as registered and 0.463 with left and right ROIs swapped. Both GLM comparisons favour the flip, weakly; the per-region FC-SC comparison (fig3e section, 0.661 against 0.407) favours no flip, by more. No flip is kept, as the stronger evidence and the one computed on the quantity the FC claims use; the conflict is recorded with the assumption. This outcome does not depend on it: neither orientation gives a negative voxel, and the activation test covers LAL and IPS on both sides (IPS on both sides only under JFRC2010, where both pass reading a), and FB and GNG lie on the midline.

Connectome-only claims (data elsewhere)¶

These are tested on the paper's per-ROI tables in its Zenodo record (hemiroi_postsyncount.mat, hemiroi_fw0sr140_transmitter.mat), which the paper computed from the FlyEM and FlyWire synapses in the template; recounting from the raw connectomes was not done (a deviation).

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's. No SPM12 motion or slice-timing correction was applied (claims file M1), so every FC and GLM result here rests on uncorrected data. The motion check shows that the raw series moves: the tdTomato in-plane shift has a median of 0.6 to 3.2 um and a 95th percentile of 2.8 to 6.1 um per fly, against a voxel of about 2.6 um. Regressing the shifts out changes the fig3d values by 0.005. The mean green image is registered to the template with ANTs SyN in Python and the ROI means are computed through the registration's linear map; tCompCor is taken from native voxels; the GLM has no Tukey-taper pre-whitening and is smoothed on the beta maps. The FC gives a lower FC-SC correlation than the paper's own output files (0.566 against 0.684 for FlyWire), and the walking map correlates with the paper's deposited map at r = 0.36 voxel by voxel. A seeded registration now repeats exactly. A registration with another seed (11) lands elsewhere: it moves native voxels by a median of 2.5 to 44 um per fly and its ROI series correlate with the first at a median of 0.18 to 0.98 (data check), yet fig3d and fig3e keep their outcomes under it. The left-right orientation rests on the per-region FC check, which the two GLM checks contradict weakly.

What was found about the dataset. The files match their description (9 flies, 3384 volumes at 1.8797 Hz, 50 Hz FicTrac, 1800 s), the walking regressor of the paper's code is reproduced to 1e-5 from the files in name order, and the seventh fly in name order (fly-100) has the lowest coverage of the hemibrain ROIs (9 ROIs partly outside the field of view, AL(L) 55% inside; the next lowest, fly-105, has 2 ROIs at 99%), which fits the paper's reason for leaving one fly out. The dimension attribute of the functional series is [128, 256, 49] while the data are stored as (time, 256, 128, 49). The ROI atlases of the paper's main analyses (SCKm, DistKm) are not published with the code or on Zenodo.
